To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the oxidation of the azodicarboxylates is reversible only in the presence of the ruthenium(II) centers, (2) the bridging ligands behave innocently, and (3) the mixed-valent intermediates are EPR silent.
the azodicarboxylate bridge is innocent, and that this is the first time that an innocently behaving bridge has been found in a mixed-valent compound with antiferromagnetical coupling.
the azodicarboxylate ligands in diruthenium complexes exhibit innocent behavior in the mixed-valent state, whereas in the fully oxidized and fully reduced states the ligand is noninnocent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, structure, and redox behavior of diruthenium complexes with bridging ligands of the azodicarboxylate type, and the bridging ligands are found to be innocent in the mixed-valent state.
the question of the identity of the intermediates in redox processes of metal complexes bridged by ligands that are able to change their oxidation state.
the synthesis and characterization of new azo-bridging ligands, the study of the corresponding diruthenium complexes, and the elucidation of the redox chemistry of these complexes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

azodicarboxylate bridged diruthenien complexes with a single azodicarboxylation bridge are innocent, whereas the presence of an additional bridging azodicarboxilation unit causes the bridging ligand to become noninnocent.
the azo-bridge is a mixed-valent ligand in the Ru(III)-Ru(II) series, whereas it is innocent in the Ru(II)-Ru(II)-Ru(I) and Ru(I)-Ru(I) series.
azo-bridges behave as innocent bridging ligands in the case of Ru(II) and Ru(III) complexes and as noninnocent in the case of the Ru(II) complexes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
azo-bridges are innocent in the case of diruthenium complexes but noninnocent in the case of dinuclear ruthenium(II) complexes.
the bridging ligands in the diruthenium complexes are innocent for the first reduction step, but noninnocent for the second reduction step.

the azodicarboxylate ligand is innocent in the Ru(III)-Ru(III) complexes and in the Ru(II)-Ru(II) compounds with the azo bridge in the neutral state, whereas the azo bridge becomes noninnocent when it is reduced to the dianionic state.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of an odd electron does not automatically lead to the noninnocent character of the bridging ligand, but rather the nature of the metal centers, the metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) character of the electronic transitions, and the ligand field strength of the metal ions are crucial parameters.

the presence of EPR signals in the reduced complexes is not a reliable criterion to decide about the noninnocence of the bridge, but the presence of NIR absorptions is a good indicator for the innocent character of the bridging ligand.

the bridging ligands in the azo-bridges are always innocent, even in the presence of strong electron acceptor and donor centers, while the diiminoacyl hydrazide ligands are noninnocent, and the odd-electron is localized on the bridging ligand.
